profile_text.body:
Coursera describes itself as a platform for online courses, Professional Certificates, Specializations, and degrees, aimed at job-ready skills. It says its catalog includes offerings from Google, Meta, Anthropic, DeepLearning.AI, IBM, and Stanford, among others, and it markets Coursera Plus as an annual subscription giving unlimited access to thousands of courses, Specializations, and Professional Certificates. The company is a for-profit public company founded in 2012, headquartered in Mountain View, California, and trades under the ticker COUR.

Its site groups much of its best-known material around AI, data science, cybersecurity, and software engineering. Named programs include the Machine Learning Specialization, the Deep Learning Specialization, the AI Essentials Specialization, the AI Engineer Professional Certificate, the Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate, the Google Project Management Professional Certificate, the Google UX Design Professional Certificate, the IBM Data Science Professional Certificate, the IBM Data Analyst Professional Certificate, the Data Analysis with Python Specialization, and the UI/UX Design Specialization. The site also points learners toward beginner-level Python and generative AI courses and toward browsing broader areas such as artificial intelligence, SQL, and web development.

Company records list a CIK of 0001651562 and a litigation exposure count of 281 in California. No products or MCP servers are tracked for the company, and no individual cases are listed.
